comments.text: Every single tech company is pulling this crap. 3D printer companies that said they were open source are now locking things down. They sucker people into buying their product, and then they change the ToS *after* you own the item. This is what really ticks me off. A sale is a sale. Once the sale is complete the terms and conditions should not be allowed to change unless both parties agree. But the language in these documents states they can change their terms whenever they like, and if you don't like it you have to stop using 'their' product (so they still claim ownership). Windows is especially egregious. Now with age verification laws happening, every OS is forced to comply, but instead of doing their own age verification we're seeing third-party companies getting that information. I'm sorry, but with the lack of security and no consumer protection laws to back up consumers, I would never want a young child's information provided to these companies. Microsoft servers are *not* secure. They've been hacked many times. Never mind the third-party servers. The last place you want to store sensitive information is in cloud storage, because that's the first place hackers get into. They don't hack your home computer for a single person's info. They hack bulk storage. They go where they're going to get the most bang for their buck. Millions of people's information is stored there, and becomes instantly theirs the moment they break through. But they're still pushing all of this stuff on consumers under the guise of convenience. We have an EV, and I'm really hoping it doesn't get hit with this garbage. If they had been up front about ongoing costs on a lot of these things, consumers wouldn't be so angry. It's the dishonesty and sneakiness. If you're going to sell a printer, 3D or otherwise, the rules shouldn't be changed after you own it. Except we don't actually own anything anymore. Our Windows PCs are advertising to us, on devices we paid for. We're not getting ad revenue, so why are we getting ads on an owned device? It takes me two days to set up a new computer because of all the garbage I have to turn off. I don't want client files on cloud servers. It's my job to maintain that confidentiality if I do someone's books (I was an accountant, and had files on my laptop at one time...thankfully I don't do that work now). Lawyers have been using cloud storage, which blows my mind. So much for due diligence and client confidentiality.
